ABSTRACT

The  Internet  of  Things  (IoT)  became  the  most  impactful  development worldwide.  This  development  influenced  many  businesses  to  adapt  and  shift  to online  business  or  so-called  e-commerce. Amazon  as  an  e-commerce  platform offered hundreds of millions of products for sales, as on June 20th, 2017 offered 372 million products online [1]. With this amount of products, amazon used the Robotic  Mobile  Fulfillment  System  (RMFS)  as  their  warehouse  system.  In  this study,  a  simulation  of  the  RMFS  was  built  used  NetLogo  to  maximize  the  pod utilization and minimize the energy consumption of the warehouse.

This  study  combined  3  SKU  to  Pod  assignments  and  4  Replenishment policies. SKU to Pod has the role to improve the pod utilization by increase pick unit  in  each  visit.  Pod  with  more  SKU  types  is  likely  to  fulfill  more  orders. Replenishment policy has the role to maintain the inventory of the warehouse and keep the pod at a high service level. Other than that, replenishment triggers reduced visits to the picking station. A pod that doesn't have sufficient capacity couldn't be assigned with new order although it already has the most order assigned.

This approach showed improvement by assigned different SKU classes in one pod and considering SKU inventory also with pod urgency level. Maintained the inventory level in the warehouse above 59% of total inventory influenced the warehouse performance. There was increasing of 17.83% in pod utilization and reducing of 14.75% in energy consumption.
Keywords :  Robotic  Mobile  Fulfillment  System  (RMFS),  Pod  Replenishment, SKUs Classification, Pod Utilization

CHAPTER 1
INTRODUCTION
1.1 Background and Motivation

In  these  past  few  years,  the  Internet  of  Things  (IoT)  became  the  most impactful development worldwide. This development influenced many businesses to  adapt  and  shift  to  online  business  or  so-called  e-commerce. As  an  example, Amazon as an e-commerce platform offered hundreds of millions of products for sales, as on June 20th, 2017 offered 372 million products online [1]. These types of products are stored in a warehouse with proper design that considering warehouse management, inventory management, and the internet of things [2].

Warehouse design has a role to maintain and improve efficiency also reduce distribution costs in the warehouse [3]. There are five main groups of warehouse systems as 'picker-to-parts', 'pick-to-box', 'pick-and-sort', 'parts-to-picker', and 'completely automated picking' [4]. In parts-to-picker warehouse integrated with the Internet of Things such as data management, sensors, robot, and many other things to synchronized all processes in the warehouse.

Robotic  Mobile  Fulfillment  System  (RMFS)  is  one  breakthrough  in  the implementation of e-commerce warehouses and is categorized as the parts-to-picker system. Kiva System as one of the innovative approaches uses hundreds of custombuilt mobile robots (AGVs) that carry small shelving units (Pods) and deliver to the assigned stations (Picking or Replenishment Station) [5]. AGVs are designed to lifting the pod, a sensing system to avoid the collision, a navigation system to help the movement of AGV, powered by battery, trolley mounted rubber wheels, and a control system as the brain of the robot [6]. Picking stations have a role to fulfill the picking order and send the products out of the warehouse. Replenishment stations have a role to maintain the product's availability in the warehouse.

The combination of the picking and replenishment station is also supported by the pods' design. Pods are assigned by the types of SKUs and amount of SKUs quantity  stored  inside  it.  This  policy  is  designed  to  maximize  the  picking  and replenishment process.  SKUs dimensions, cycles, characteristics, and popularity are considered as a factor to assign SKUs to pods [7].  The SKUs need to distribute in all pods with a policy such as :

Pod utilization is measured base on the SKU's capability to maintain a high picking unit/ visit. Replenishment policy is designed to avoid stock out of SKUs which can delay the orders fulfillment and reduce pod utilization. In a traditional warehouse or 'pickers-to-parts' replenishment is always triggered by each SKU's inventory level. If the inventory level of the SKU reached a certain level it will order a certain quantity [12, 13]. However, the RMFS's replenishment considered pod condition which contained many types of SKUs. Pod condition is influenced base on the pod's location, the pod's free space, the pod's frequency being picked, and  the  pod's  inventory  level  of  an  SKU  is  considered  as  the  trigger  for  the replenishment  [14,  15].  After  the  pod  was  triggered  to  be  replenished,  AGV delivered the pod to the replenishment station. AGV's could be assigned only for the  picking/replenishment  process  [14]  or  both  processes.  This  assignment  also influenced the time for the pod to get replenishment.

In  this  study,  SKUs  assignment  to  pods  designed  to  maximize  the  pod utilization. ABC classification was implemented to assign SKUs in pods based on demand popularity. Replenishment policy designed to maintain inventory level of the pod. The replenishment is triggered based on the SKUs urgency in the pod. Furthermore, by combined these assignments the warehouse could have a reduction in energy consumption and increase pod utilization.
1.2 Objective

The  objective  of  this  study  is  to  minimize  energy  consumption  and maximize  pod utilization by considering the inventory level.  The energy consumption considered the average number of pods delivered to the picking station in an hour. The fewer pods delivered to the picking station means the AGVs didn't need to move around the warehouse too much. Other than that, fewer pods delivered need to maximize the pod utilization for maintaining the throughput efficiency of the warehouse.

The pod utilization considered the average number of SKUs being pick in each visit. Designed the combination of SKU types to increase more SKUs being picked in each visit. More SKUs being picked indicate that the pod quantity got to reduce a lot. Low pod capacity influenced the total number of orders being pick in each  visit.  This  is  maintained  by  determined  the  replenishment  policy  and  the replenishment level of the pod. Combined the SKU to pod assignment with the replenishment policy influenced the objectives. The combined scenario is explained in more detail in chapter 3.
1.3 Scope and Limitation

Few limitations are being used in this study. First, all AGVs are assigned for the  picking  and  replenishment  process. This  means AGVs  didn't  divide  to  only assigned to the picking/replenishment process. Second, all SKUs need to be store in the warehouse. Although there are SKUs rarely being order, it's still being stored in the warehouse. Third, SKU was differentiated by SKU types and number of units. Fourth, the AGV charging process is not yet to be considered, thus focusing on the picking and replenishment process. Fifth, the warehouse simulated using NetLogo as  the  main  platform  of  Agent-Based  Modelling  (ABM).  This  simulation  also integrated with python as the optimization platform and excel as the data database for storing the result from NetLogo and python.
1.4 Organization of Thesis

This  study  consist  of  five  chapters.  The  organization  of  it  is  as  follows: Chapter 1 presents the problem background and motivation of the study, as well as the objective, and scope also limitation. Chapter 2 explains the literature review of related  work. Chapter 3 describes the simulation platform, its process flow, and parameters. Chapter 4 analyze the proposed improvement, including the result of it; and Chapter 5 conclusion and future work for this study.
CHAPTER 2
LITERATURE REVIEW
2.1 Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems (RMFS)

RMFS is one of the breakthroughs  in  warehouse  systems  to  adapt  to  ecommerce disruption. This system is  supported  by AGVs, Pods, Replenishment Station, Picking Station, and Charging Stations. AGVs have the role bring the pod to picking or replenishment stations then bring the pod back to the storage area, one of the advantages of this system is eliminating the need for humans movement in the storage area [14, 16]. Pods have the role of SKU storage which is divided into few compartments. AGV can carry a pod with a weight of around 450 - 1300 kg depends on the pod size [17]. An example of AGV carries the pod is shown in Figure 1.

The process of RMFS started when there is an order enter the system. There are 2 types of order, picking order and replenishment order. Picking order assigned to the pod which has the required SKU. AGV picked the pod from its location and delivered it to the picking station. After finishing the picking process, AGV brought back  the  pod  to  the  empty  location  in  the  storage  area.  Replenishment  order  is triggered when the pod already reaches a certain inventory level [15]. An illustration of the RMFS process is shown in Figure 2.

In layout design, it determined based on the total working stations, total pods, total AGVs, and total SKU capacity. In SKUs distribution, it needs to consider the total types of SKUs and the pod's capacity. SKUs assignment has a role to support the operation stage later on. By designing all of these considerations RMFS  can  be synchronized to maximize warehouse performance.
2.2 SKUs to Pods Assignment

SKUs to Pods assignment described as SKUs distribution to all pods that limited with single type SKU in one pod or multiple types SKU in one pod. This assignment influenced the number of units being picked from the shelf. 3 problems were considered like SKU's types in one pod, SKU quantity in one pod, and SKU distribution in other pods [21, 22]. After considering these factors SKUs can be assigned as single SKU in one pod and multiple SKUs in one pod (mixed shelves). Single SKU in one pod is suitable when there are large quantity orders, however, mixed shelves are more suitable in e-commerce which has small quantity orders [18].

Multiple SKUs can be assigned randomly or following a policy to one pod. Many policies can be used like SKU similarity [8, 9, 23], Association Rules, and ABC classification [11]. In SKUs similarity, the pod require to maximize all SKUs similarity. In Association Rules it has the same objective of SKUs similarity, but it will consider the most frequent combination of the SKUs. 2.3 ABC Classification

ABC Classification is a method to classified a large number of products (SKUs)  based  on  specific  criteria.  The  cost  criteria  based  on  minimizing  total inventory cost consider the shortage cost of demand divided by holding cost of the order size [24]. ABC classification has the similarity with Pareto's Law where 20% of  total  effort  yields  80%  total  of  outcome  [25].  Multiple  criteria  in  the ABC Classification design are in table 1.

Implementation of ABC classification used in inventory with a large number of SKUs. Class A which referred to SKUs with high urgency needs to be prioritized in the warehouse, class B has less priority, and class C has the lowest priority [28]. Inventory management can be design based on the priority of each class to gain a high  service  level  of  the  warehouse. Although  class  C  has  the  least  priority  a countermeasure needs to be designed to avoid stock out.
2.4 Inventory Management

Inventory management has an important role in the warehouse management system.  The  main  purpose  is  to  maintain  the  availability  of  the  product  in  the warehouse.  A  replenishment  strategy  which  not  design  properly  can  lead  to overstock or stock out in the warehouse, and this can make a bullwhip effect or disruption to the entire supply chain process [28]. There are 3 indicators that are considered as the inventory level in the replenishment schedule [29].

3.2 Process Flow
RMFS process is divided into few parts based on the relation from each resource. The RMFS process flow can be seen in figure 5.
Figure 5. RMFS Process Flow and The Relation Between Each Resource.
Figure 5. RMFS Process Flow and The Relation Between Each Resource.

There are 6 resources described such as order, SKU, pod, robot (AGVs), picking station, and replenishment station. Between each resource, it started with SKU to Pod assignment, order arrival, order to pod assignment, pod sequencing, robot  to  pod  assignment,  robot  routing,  robot  to  stations  (Picking  station  and replenishment station), robot to storage assignment, pod to replenish, and SKU to replenish. Each process is described in more detail in the next sub-chapter.
3.2.1 SKU to Pod Assignment

SKU  to  pod  assignment  needs  to  be  determined  before  operating  the warehouse. This study used 3 scenarios, Random used as the baseline, One Pod One Class, and Mix Class One Pod assignment. However, the limitation in this study is all the SKUs need to be stored in pods. Random assignment randomly assigns the SKU to the pod based on the SKU limit in the pod. One class one pod, use ABC rule to classify the number of pods based on 60% pod of SKU A, 25% pod of SKU B, 15% pod of SKU C. Mix class one pod, ABC rule to classify the number of units based on 60% units of SKU A, 25% units of SKU B, 15% units of SKU C. The detail about SKU distribution is explained in more detail in chapter 4.
3.2.2 Order Arrival

First,  generate  the  arrival  time  following  a  certain  distribution.  In  each arrival, it  generated  few orders with 1 type of SKU. The total amount of orders generated are between 1 and 2 [15]. The type of SKU is based on the following ABC rule where 10% of the SKU is 60% of the order, 30% of the SKU is 25% of the order, and 60% of the SKU is 15% of the order.
3.2.3 Order to Pod Assignment

After  the  order  is  generated  it  is  assigned  to  the  pod  immediately.  The generated order is assigned to the pod which has the earliest due-date order. After the  pod  decided,  it  checked  the  capacity  of  the  SKU  of  the  order.  SKU  with sufficient capacity picked as the order to pod result otherwise, it checked another pod to assigned. This means one pod could have more than 1 order.
3.2.4 Pod Sequencing

After the order is  assigned  to  the  pod  it  sorted  the  pod  based  on  certain criteria. The system sorted the pod based on the earliest due date of the order. This process has the function to determine the urgency of the order in the pod.
3.2.5 Robot to Pod Assignment
After the order being assigned to the pod, it is labeled as the selected pod.

Available AGVs are assigned to pick the selected pod with the earliest due date and nearest  distance.  The  total  pod  that  is  being  considered  double  the  number  of available AGVs. This assignment used manhattan distance to calculate the distance [33] and the Hungarian algorithm [34] to pair the AGVs with the pods. Distance calculation  considered  all  the  possibilities  of  the  selected  pod  with  the  starting intersection and ending intersection [35]. This distance used as a value to compare in the Hungarian algorithm.
3.2.6 Robot Routing

In this simulation, the routing policy following the previous research using Simple  Routing  with  Traffic  Policy  [35].  The  AGVs  routing  is  based  on  the direction in the aisle like shown in Figure 5. Other than that, there is an exception where the AGV can move beneath the pod horizontally to the destination in the same pod batch. The traffic policy used is deadlock and collision prevention, also in each intersection AGV horizontal aisle will be prioritized.
3.2.7 Robot to Stations

AGV that is already assigned to the selected pod needs to deliver it to the station based on the order. In picking or replenishment order the AGV is assigned to the station with the least AGV waiting. Assign AGV to the station with more AGV increased the queuing time in the station.
3.2.8 Robot to Storage Assignment

After finish, the picking or replenishment process AGV needs to bring back the pod to the storage area. First, list all the possible empty locations in the storage area. This list is considered with the AGV which needs to bring back the pod. The Hungarian  algorithm  is  used  to  determine  the  nearest  empty  location  from  the station.
3.2.9 Pod to Replenish

After the pod finishes the picking process it checked the pod condition based on the policy. If the pod needs to be replenished, AGV directly delivers the pod to the  replenishment  station.  Pod  replenishment  is  triggered  by  a  certain  policy.  4 policies used in this study are the Emptiest Pod, Pod Inventory Level, Warehouse Inventory-SKU  in  Pod,  and  Stockout  Probability.  The  baseline  of  the  pod replenishment is Pod Inventory Level with a 60% inventory level.
3.2.10 SKU to Replenish

In this study, a dedicated policy was implemented for the  SKU replenishment. The SKU in the pod got replenish with the same types of SKU. Other than  that,  the  SKU  quantity  was  replenished  back  to  the  maximum  capacity.  In Warehouse Inventory-SKU in Pod replenished the SKU that need to be replenished and in other policies, it is replenished all SKUs in the pod

5.1 Conclusion

The Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS) is one breakthrough in the implementation of e-commerce warehouses and is categorized as the parts-to-picker system. This system needs to have a proper design to adapt to the e-commerce order. However,  this  system  needs  to  consider  many  factors  to  minimize  energy consumption and maximize pod utilization.

The  implementation  of  the  scenarios  of  SKU  to  Pod  assignment  and replenishment policy influenced the performance of the system. SKU to Pod has the role to improve the pod utilization by increase pick unit in each visit. Pod with more SKU types is likely to fulfill more orders. Replenishment policy has the role to maintain the inventory of the warehouse and keep the pod at a high service level. Other than that, replenishment triggers reduced visits to the picking station. A pod that doesn't have sufficient capacity couldn't be assigned with new order although it already has the most order assigned.

There are 3 scenarios in the SKU to Pod assignments such as Random and ABC Classification which is divided as One Class One Pod and Mixed Class One Pod.  There  are  4  scenarios  in  the  replenishment  policies  as  the  Emptiest,  Pod Inventory Level, Stockout Probability, and Warehouse Inventory - SKU in Pod. The baseline of this study is Random-Pod Inventory Level with a 60% inventory level. This baseline is compared with other combined scenarios to find the best result.

The result of each scenario is verified using ANOVA and Tukey Pairwise Comparison. The best result is Mixed Class One Pod combined with the Warehouse Inventory SKU in Pod. There is a slight increase of 0.56% of throughput efficiency other than that, the energy consumption reduced by 14.75% pod visit and increased the pod utilization by 17.83% compared to baseline. These results can be achieved by maintaining an average of 59.26% inventory of the warehouse.

This approach showed improvement by assigned different SKU classes in one pod and considering SKU inventory also with pod urgency level. In  these  past  few  years,  the  Internet  of  Things  (IoT)  became  the  most impactful development worldwide. This development influenced many businesses to  adapt  and  shift  to  online  business  or  so-called  e-commerce. As  an  example, Amazon as an e-commerce platform offered hundreds of millions of products for sales, as on June 20th, 2017 offered 372 million products online [1]. These types of products are stored in a warehouse with proper design that considering warehouse management, inventory management, and the internet of things [2].
Warehouse design has a role to maintain and improve efficiency also reduce distribution costs in the warehouse [3]. There are five main groups of warehouse systems as 'picker-to-parts', 'pick-to-box', 'pick-and-sort', 'parts-to-picker', and 'completely automated picking' [4]. In parts-to-picker warehouse integrated with the Internet of Things such as data management, sensors, robot, and many other things to synchronized all processes in the warehouse.

Robotic  Mobile  Fulfillment  System  (RMFS)  is  one  breakthrough  in  the implementation of e-commerce warehouses and is categorized as the parts-to-picker system. Kiva System as one of the innovative approaches uses hundreds of custombuilt mobile robots (AGVs) that carry small shelving units (Pods) and deliver to the assigned stations (Picking or Replenishment Station) [5]. AGVs are designed to lifting the pod, a sensing system to avoid the collision, a navigation system to help the movement of AGV, powered by battery, trolley mounted rubber wheels, and a control system as the brain of the robot [6]. Picking stations have a role to fulfill the picking order and send the products out of the warehouse. Replenishment stations have a role to maintain the product's availability in the warehouse.

The combination of the picking and replenishment station is also supported by the pods' design. Pods are assigned by the types of SKUs and amount of SKUs quantity  stored  inside  it.  This  policy  is  designed  to  maximize  the  picking  and replenishment process.  SKUs dimensions, cycles, characteristics, and popularity are considered as a factor to assign SKUs to pods [7].  The SKUs need to distribute in all pods with a policy such as :

1. Random, SKU assigned to the pod with random order.
2. Product similarity, integrated with order batching or order alienation to consider the product similarity by considering 2 - 40 SKUs [8] [9].
3. Association Rules (AR), considering orders pattern as the base for correlation between the SKUs and give a combination of SKUs that can be assigned in the pod. Implement this method with a small number of SKUs ( 10 SKUs [10] and 26 SKUs [11] ) can give feasible results, however, if a large number of SKUs being considered it showed an unfeasible combination.
4. ABC classification,  SKU  assigned  base  on  the  popularity  proportion  of  the SKUs.  Integrating  AR  and  ABC  classification  is  used  to  design  the    SKUs assignment to pod by set class-A's SKUs in all the pod and correlated with other classes also SKU with promotional effect [11].

Pod utilization is measured base on the SKU's capability to maintain a high picking unit/ visit. Replenishment policy is designed to avoid stock out of SKUs which can delay the orders fulfillment and reduce pod utilization. In a traditional warehouse or 'pickers-to-parts' replenishment is always triggered by each SKU's inventory level. If the inventory level of the SKU reached a certain level it will order a certain quantity [12, 13]. However, the RMFS's replenishment considered pod condition which contained many types of SKUs. Pod condition is influenced base on the pod's location, the pod's free space, the pod's frequency being picked, and  the  pod's  inventory  level  of  an  SKU  is  considered  as  the  trigger  for  the replenishment  [14,  15].  After  the  pod  was  triggered  to  be  replenished,  AGV delivered the pod to the replenishment station. AGV's could be assigned only for the  picking/replenishment  process  [14]  or  both  processes.  This  assignment  also influenced the time for the pod to get replenishment.

In  this  study,  SKUs  assignment  to  pods  designed  to  maximize  the  pod utilization. ABC classification was implemented to assign SKUs in pods based on demand popularity. Replenishment policy designed to maintain inventory level of the pod. The replenishment is triggered based on the SKUs urgency in the pod. Furthermore, by combined these assignments the warehouse could have a reduction in energy consumption and increase pod utilization.

The  objective  of  this  study  is  to  minimize  energy  consumption  and maximize  pod utilization by considering the inventory level.  The energy consumption considered the average number of pods delivered to the picking station in an hour. The fewer pods delivered to the picking station means the AGVs didn't need to move around the warehouse too much. Other than that, fewer pods delivered need to maximize the pod utilization for maintaining the throughput efficiency of the warehouse.
The pod utilization considered the average number of SKUs being pick in each visit. Designed the combination of SKU types to increase more SKUs being picked in each visit. More SKUs being picked indicate that the pod quantity got to reduce a lot. Low pod capacity influenced the total number of orders being pick in each  visit.  This  is  maintained  by  determined  the  replenishment  policy  and  the replenishment level of the pod. Combined the SKU to pod assignment with the replenishment policy influenced the objectives. The combined scenario is explained in more detail in chapter 3.

Few limitations are being used in this study. First, all AGVs are assigned for the  picking  and  replenishment  process. This  means AGVs  didn't  divide  to  only assigned to the picking/replenishment process. Second, all SKUs need to be store in the warehouse. Although there are SKUs rarely being order, it's still being stored in the warehouse. Third, SKU was differentiated by SKU types and number of units. Fourth, the AGV charging process is not yet to be considered, thus focusing on the picking and replenishment process. Fifth, the warehouse simulated using NetLogo as  the  main  platform  of  Agent-Based  Modelling  (ABM). In  RMFS implementation  there  is  also  a  preparation  stage  to  design  the warehouse.  Few  things  need  to  be  considered  like  the  layout  design  and  SKU distribution. In layout design, it determined based on the total working stations, total pods, total AGVs, and total SKU capacity. In SKUs distribution, it needs to consider the total types of SKUs and the pod's capacity. SKUs assignment has a role to support the operation stage later on. In the operation stage there are 5 assignments referred to as decision problems in RMFS [14] :

1. Pick Order Assignment (POA), selecting the picking order to be assigned to the pod first.
2. Replenishment Order Assignment (ROA), selecting replenishment station for next order.
3. Pick Pod Selection (PPS), selecting pod to transport to a pick station.
4. Replenishment Pod Selection (RPS), selecting pod to get replenished.
5. Pod Storage Assignment (PSA), selecting empty storage location for the pod.
Other than these assignments RMFS also focuses in set the routing of the AGVs. Path planning is the most popular method in this by generating a path that is followed by the robot [14]. Other than these assignments RMFS also focuses in set the routing of the AGVs. Path planning is the most popular method in this by generating a path that is followed by the robot  [18, 19, 20]. By designing all of these considerations RMFS  can  be synchronized to maximize warehouse performance.

SKUs to Pods assignment described as SKUs distribution to all pods that limited with single type SKU in one pod or multiple types SKU in one pod. This assignment influenced the number of units being picked from the shelf. 3 problems were considered like SKU's types in one pod, SKU quantity in one pod, and SKU distribution in other pods [21, 22]. After considering these factors SKUs can be assigned as single SKU in one pod and multiple SKUs in one pod (mixed shelves). Single SKU in one pod is suitable when there are large quantity orders, however, mixed shelves are more suitable in e-commerce which has small quantity orders [18].

In SKUs similarity, the pod require to maximize all SKUs similarity. In Association Rules it has the same objective of SKUs similarity, but it will consider the most frequent combination of the SKUs. Inventory management has an important role in the warehouse management system.  The  main  purpose  is  to  maintain  the  availability  of  the  product  in  the warehouse.  A  replenishment  strategy  which  not  design  properly  can  lead  to overstock or stock out in the warehouse, and this can make a bullwhip effect or disruption to the entire supply chain process [28]. Following  the indicator, replenishment levels need to be set to determine the minimum level and the number to be replenished. Few replenishment policies can be used such as [12, 13, 30, 31, 32]:

2. 'Q, S' policy is the total amount of demand since the previous order reaches Q units, an order of amount Q to raises the inventory positions of all items to S.
3. 's,  Q'  policy  is  a  joint  replenishment  order  of  size  Q  is  triggered  when  the inventory position of an item falls to its reorder point s.
4. 'R, nQ' policy is a periodic review of inventory position and order minimum inventory position to be at or above R.
5. Stock-Need Rule policy is the lower the stock level of a product compared to the needs of the product in a certain wave.

SKU  to  pod  assignment  needs  to  be  determined  before  operating  the warehouse. This study used 3 scenarios, Random used as the baseline, One Pod One Class, and Mix Class One Pod assignment. However, the limitation in this study is all the SKUs need to be stored in pods. Random assignment randomly assigns the SKU to the pod based on the SKU limit in the pod. One class one pod, use ABC rule to classify the number of pods based on 60% pod of SKU A, 25% pod of SKU B, 15% pod of SKU C. Mix class one pod, ABC rule to classify the number of units based on 60% units of SKU A, 25% units of SKU B, 15% units of SKU C. The detail about SKU distribution is explained in more detail in chapter 4.

First,  generate  the  arrival  time  following  a  certain  distribution.  In  each arrival, it  generated  few orders with 1 type of SKU. The total amount of orders generated are between 1 and 2 [15]. The type of SKU is based on the following ABC rule where 10% of the SKU is 60% of the order, 30% of the SKU is 25% of the order, and 60% of the SKU is 15% of the order.

After  the  order  is  generated  it  is  assigned  to  the  pod  immediately.  The generated order is assigned to the pod which has the earliest due-date order. After the  pod  decided,  it  checked  the  capacity  of  the  SKU  of  the  order.  SKU  with sufficient capacity picked as the order to pod result otherwise, it checked another pod to assigned. This means one pod could have more than 1 order.

After the order is  assigned  to  the  pod  it  sorted  the  pod  based  on  certain criteria. The system sorted the pod based on the earliest due date of the order. This process has the function to determine the urgency of the order in the pod.

After the order being assigned to the pod, it is labeled as the selected pod.
Available AGVs are assigned to pick the selected pod with the earliest due date and nearest  distance.  The  total  pod  that  is  being  considered  double  the  number  of available AGVs. This assignment used manhattan distance to calculate the distance [33] and the Hungarian algorithm [34] to pair the AGVs with the pods. Distance calculation  considered  all  the  possibilities  of  the  selected  pod  with  the  starting intersection and ending intersection [35]. This distance used as a value to compare in the Hungarian algorithm.

In this simulation, the routing policy following the previous research using Simple  Routing  with  Traffic  Policy  [35].  The  AGVs  routing  is  based  on  the direction in the aisle like shown in Figure 5. Other than that, there is an exception where the AGV can move beneath the pod horizontally to the destination in the same pod batch. The traffic policy used is deadlock and collision prevention, also in each intersection AGV horizontal aisle will be prioritized.

AGV that is already assigned to the selected pod needs to deliver it to the station based on the order. In picking or replenishment order the AGV is assigned to the station with the least AGV waiting. Assign AGV to the station with more AGV increased the queuing time in the station.

After finish, the picking or replenishment process AGV needs to bring back the pod to the storage area. First, list all the possible empty locations in the storage area. This list is considered with the AGV which needs to bring back the pod. The Hungarian  algorithm  is  used  to  determine  the  nearest  empty  location  from  the station.

After the pod finishes the picking process it checked the pod condition based on the policy. If the pod needs to be replenished, AGV directly delivers the pod to the  replenishment  station.  Pod  replenishment  is  triggered  by  a  certain  policy.  4 policies used in this study are the Emptiest Pod, Pod Inventory Level, Warehouse Inventory-SKU  in  Pod,  and  Stockout  Probability.  The  baseline  of  the  pod replenishment is Pod Inventory Level with a 60% inventory level.

In this study, a dedicated policy was implemented for the  SKU replenishment. The SKU in the pod got replenish with the same types of SKU. Other than  that,  the  SKU  quantity  was  replenished  back  to  the  maximum  capacity.  In Warehouse Inventory-SKU in Pod replenished the SKU that need to be replenished and in other policies, it is replenished all SKUs in the pod

The Robotic Mobile Fulfillment System (RMFS) is one breakthrough in the implementation of e-commerce warehouses and is categorized as the parts-to-picker system. This system needs to have a proper design to adapt to the e-commerce order. However,  this  system  needs  to  consider  many  factors  to  minimize  energy consumption and maximize pod utilization.
The  implementation  of  the  scenarios  of  SKU  to  Pod  assignment  and replenishment policy influenced the performance of the system. SKU to Pod has the role to improve the pod utilization by increase pick unit in each visit. Pod with more SKU types is likely to fulfill more orders. Replenishment policy has the role to maintain the inventory of the warehouse and keep the pod at a high service level. Other than that, replenishment triggers reduced visits to the picking station. A pod that doesn't have sufficient capacity couldn't be assigned with new order although it already has the most order assigned.

There are 3 scenarios in the SKU to Pod assignments such as Random and ABC Classification which is divided as One Class One Pod and Mixed Class One Pod.  There  are  4  scenarios  in  the  replenishment  policies  as  the  Emptiest,  Pod Inventory Level, Stockout Probability, and Warehouse Inventory - SKU in Pod. The baseline of this study is Random-Pod Inventory Level with a 60% inventory level. This baseline is compared with other combined scenarios to find the best result.
The result of each scenario is verified using ANOVA and Tukey Pairwise Comparison. The best result is Mixed Class One Pod combined with the Warehouse Inventory SKU in Pod. There is a slight increase of 0.56% of throughput efficiency other than that, the energy consumption reduced by 14.75% pod visit and increased the pod utilization by 17.83% compared to baseline. These results can be achieved by maintaining an average of 59.26% inventory of the warehouse.
There  are  many  possibilities  in  this  RMFS  research  that  still  can  be developed. The replenishment policy can implement flexible replenishment of SKU

to  the  pod. The pod can get replenished by a new type of SKU.  Replacing less popular SKUs with more popular SKUs can increase pod utilization. In SKU to pod assignment can research by considering the product volume and weight. These two considerations can decide the number of the compartment in a pod. Furthermore, the AGV's energy consumption can influence by the pod weight. Which heavier pod requires more energy.
